title: Evolution of Commonsense Knowledge Graphs and Reasoning Benchmarks (2013–2021)
summary: This community centers on the development of commonsense knowledge resources, tracing a lineage from early semantic parsing and web-based knowledge bases to specialized commonsense graphs like ATOMIC and ConceptNet5. It highlights the transition from symbolic representations to neural approaches, exemplified by the (Comet-) Atomic 2020 paper. The cluster also includes key evaluation benchmarks such as CommonsenseQA, SocialIQA, and PIQA, which test models' ability to reason about social and physical commonsense.
key_findings: ATOMIC, proposed by Maarten Sap, Yejin Choi, and others, is a commonsense knowledge graph modeling causal relationships, published at AAAI 2019.
The (Comet-) Atomic 2020 paper by Jena D. Hwang, Chandra Bhagavatula, and Yejin Choi discusses the integration of symbolic and neural commonsense knowledge graphs.
CommonsenseQA, authored by Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, and Jonathan Berant, is a question answering challenge specifically targeting commonsense knowledge.
SocialIQA, authored by Maarten Sap, Ronan LeBras, and Yejin Choi, is a dataset designed for commonsense reasoning about social interactions.
PIQA, authored by Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, and Yejin Choi, focuses on reasoning about physical commonsense in natural language and was published at AAAI 2020.

Jonathan Berant and Alon Talmor contributed to earlier foundational work, including 'The Web as a Knowledge-Base for Answering Complex Questions' (NAACL-HLT 2018) and 'Semantic Parsing on Freebase' (EMNLP 2013).
